answer: Because the vertex index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the bridge audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the plume identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator burns for 228 runs and collects one. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 228 answers need 228 separate inference runs with separate seeds. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
